Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
rho...@hamilton.edu (Harpua J. Howard) writes:

>although this can be a pain in the ass to pull off, the proper combat deck
>can do it.

>get basillia out. (so what if she's expensive...play a minion tap)

>put a potence master card on her (gives her sup. potence)

>when you get into combat, have a press ready (mob connections) and don't
>do agg. damage the first round, use a zip gun or something really stupid
>(try to be funny). but before range is determined play torn sign post and
>fists of death so they think something big is coming (then use the zip
>gun- don't manuever)

>second round (be at close range!)

>hand strike with undead strengh, growing fury, lucky blow.... or whatever
>you have in your hand.

>if you now follow my logic, you just did up to 11 points of Agg. damage
>depending on how many cards you had access to. this will BURN most any
>vamp. (assuming you hit)

Each of Undead Strength, Growing Fury, and Lucky Blow are strikes. You
can only use one. (Even with celerity-induced multiple strikes, the first
one that landed would send the opposition to torpor before any further
strikes connect.) Max damage=6 agg. (Torn Signpost and Growing Fury).

Respectable, but not as daunting as 11agg.
L.Scott

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
la...@bu.edu (Larry Harriman) writes:

>The sengir dagger reads "if any card adds additional damage, this too

>is aggravated" or something very similar.

Indeed it does. But the Sengir Dagger is a melee weapon, and card that
affect only hand damage don't affect it. Torn Signpost and Fists of Death
affect hand damage, not melee damage. Max damage with Sengir is 4 (with
Growing Fury).
Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)
